summary: SYNC STILL BROKEN AT UI LEVEL. Real-browser Playwright drove production URLs and confirmed that api.pizzadenfert.fr emits duplicated Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers on non-OPTIONS responses, which every modern browser refuses. Consequence: NO browser (customer app pizzadenfert.fr, admin console admin.pizzadenfert.fr, or loyalty kiosk loyalty.pizzadenfert.fr) can successfully POST/GET against api.pizzadenfert.fr. Iteration_14's curl-based 'verified' status was a false positive — curl ignores CORS. Two ACAO headers are being emitted simultaneously: '*' (from FastAPI CORSMiddleware) AND the echoed request Origin (from nginx add_header ... always).
final_verdict: SYNC STILL BROKEN AT UI LEVEL: duplicated Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers ('*' from FastAPI + '<origin>' from nginx) on GET/POST responses cause all browsers to block every fetch to api.pizzadenfert.fr.

cors_evidence.why_iteration_14_missed_it: iteration_14 verified CORS only on OPTIONS preflight (which nginx short-circuits and only emits one ACAO). It never issued the *actual* GET/POST from a browser, so it missed that FastAPI's CORSMiddleware ALSO adds its own ACAO on 2xx/4xx responses, resulting in TWO ACAO headers on real requests.

critical.endpoint: ALL /api/* GET & POST responses on api.pizzadenfert.fr
critical.issue: Duplicated Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers (one '*' from FastAPI CORSMiddleware, one echoed origin from nginx add_header). Every browser rejects the response with 'multiple values ... but only one is allowed'. Effectively no browser can call the API. Fix: remove either the FastAPI-side CORSMiddleware OR the nginx add_header block for /api/*. Recommended: keep FastAPI-side CORS with an explicit allow_origins list [https://pizzadenfert.fr, https://admin.pizzadenfert.fr, https://loyalty.pizzadenfert.fr] and delete the nginx add_header Access-Control-* directives for the api.pizzadenfert.fr vhost (or vice-versa). Also DELETE any duplicate access-control-allow-credentials.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: On api.pizzadenfert.fr, BOTH nginx and FastAPI add CORS headers to non-OPTIONS responses. nginx has `add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin $http_origin always;` in its vhost (introduced in iteration_14 to fix the missing api.pizzadenfert.fr host). FastAPI ALSO has CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=['*']) already installed at app startup. When the request reaches FastAPI, FastAPI adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; on the way back through nginx, nginx APPENDS another `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin>` because of the `always` flag. Browsers see two ACAO values on the same response and reject the fetch. Curl succeeds because it does not enforce CORS. OPTIONS preflight worked in iter_14 because nginx handles OPTIONS itself and shortcuts before FastAPI, producing only one ACAO. REPRODUCTION: `curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://pizzadenfert.fr' https://api.pizzadenfert.fr/api/menu | grep -i allow-origin` returns two lines. MITIGATION: Remove one of the two CORS emitters. Cleanest is to (a) remove the nginx add_header block for /api/*  and let FastAPI (with an explicit allow_origins list including https://pizzadenfert.fr, https://admin.pizzadenfert.fr, https://loyalty.pizzadenfert.fr) be the single source of truth, then reload nginx and restart FastAPI. Verify with the curl one-liner above expecting a single ACAO header, then re-run the Playwright UI tests.
